=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 102 (`exit 0`), and the `failed` variable at lines 61–100 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: The helper always exits successfully even when hide or restore detects a validation or credential-handling failure.
  WHY: Callers rely on a non-zero exit to stop the editor or subsequent Git operations, so the unconditional success lets workflows continue without safely hidden or restored credentials.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 81-83 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts a GitHub origin without verifying that it still names the workflow's authorized repository or rejecting credentials re-added to the origin.
  WHY: An editor can change the origin to an attacker-controlled GitHub repository, after which restore inserts the workflow token into that destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 35-53 and lines 76-95 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide and restore do not adequately validate `remote.origin.pushurl`, multiple origin URLs, or `url.*.pushInsteadOf` rewrites.
  WHY: A credential-bearing push URL can remain visible during editor execution or a push can be redirected to an unauthorized destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 45-49 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide records extraheader config keys verbatim in the editor-readable marker without rejecting keys that contain embedded credentials.
  WHY: A credential embedded in a config key name is written into the marker and exposed to the editor process.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 85-93 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore reapplies extraheaders at their recorded or generic GitHub scope instead of scoping them to the verified origin repository.
  WHY: The workflow token can then authenticate GitHub requests to repositories other than the intended origin.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 29-33 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide treats a subdirectory of a parent Git repository as a checkout root.
  WHY: When `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` is a non-git subdirectory, hide can strip credentials from the parent repository instead of skipping that directory.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 61-97 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore injects credentials into checkouts sequentially instead of validating every checkout before modifying any of them.
  WHY: If a later checkout fails validation, an earlier checkout may already contain the workflow token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 56 (`[ -s "${marker}" ] || exit 0`) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits successfully and silently when the marker is absent.
  WHY: Operators cannot distinguish a missing marker from a successful restore; severity was reported as both BLOCKER and MAJOR, so the higher severity is used.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 57–59 (missing GH_TOKEN in restore) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore exits successfully when `GH_TOKEN` is missing or empty.
  WHY: The workflow can continue after credentials could not be restored, while the step appears successful.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 22-24 (hide path, existing marker check) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide exits successfully when an unrestored marker already exists.
  WHY: A prior failed restore may have left credentials exposed, and proceeding can overwrite the marker needed to restore them.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 19-54 (hide path, the `for repo` loop) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide does not require a trusted `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` identity before handling checkout credentials.
  WHY: Without that identity, the helper cannot verify the repository against which credentials are hidden or restored.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 94-98 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore can apply an extraheader from the marker without a corresponding validated origin entry.
  WHY: The Authorization header can be restored without confirming that the checkout's repository remote is valid.
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py: lines 94-105 (test_restore_rejects_credentials_added_to_the_original_origin) and lines 168-178 (test_hide_does_not_record_a_secret_in_an_extraheader_key) of the LAST RUN DIFF | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The two tests added in the last run assert security checks that the helper does not implement.
  WHY: The tests fail because restore accepts an origin with editor-added credentials and hide records an extraheader key containing a credential.

=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 102 (`exit 0`) and the `failed` variable at lines 61–100 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The script always exits 0 even when `failed=true` or another error condition was detected.
  WHY: Workflow callers expect hide and restore failures to stop the editor step, but the editor can proceed without credential isolation.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 81–83 (restore origin validation) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore accepts any `https://github.com/` origin without verifying that it still names the workflow's repository.
  WHY: An editor can change origin to `https://github.com/attacker/repo.git`, causing the workflow token to be injected into that destination.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 35–43 (hide pushurl inspection) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide does not inspect or remove `remote.origin.pushurl` or check `url.*.pushInsteadOf` rewrites.
  WHY: A credential-bearing push URL or redirected push can remain available to the editor.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 45–48 (hide extraheader key recording) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide records extraheader config keys verbatim without rejecting embedded credentials.
  WHY: The editor-readable marker can expose a credential embedded in the key name.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 85–93 (restore extraheader scope) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore reapplies extraheaders at their recorded key instead of scoping them to the verified origin path.
  WHY: The workflow token can authenticate requests to repositories other than the intended origin.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 29–33 (non-checkout subdirectory) | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Hide treats a subdirectory of a parent Git repository as a checkout root.
  WHY: A non-git `GITHUB_WORKSPACE` subdirectory can cause hide to strip credentials from the parent repository.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: line 56 (`[ -s "${marker}" ] || exit 0`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore exits silently and successfully when the marker is absent.
  WHY: Operators see a successful restore without any indication that credentials were not restored.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh: lines 57–59 (missing GH_TOKEN in restore) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: Restore exits successfully when `GH_TOKEN` is missing or empty.
  WHY: The workflow can continue after a restore step that could not restore credentials.
- TASK_GAP:
  Requirement: "Hiding/restoring git auth fails the editor step on error" (PR Description, agents.md update, docs/INVENTORY.md description)
  Expected change site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh — replace unconditional `exit 0` at line 102 with a conditional exit on the `failed` flag; add non-zero exits in hide paths for existing marker, credential-bearing extraheader keys, missing GITHUB_REPOSITORY, pushurl, and pushInsteadOf; add non-zero exit in restore for missing GH_TOKEN.
  Evidence of absence: The script ends with `exit 0` (line 102). No code path exits non-zero except the usage error (exit 2 on line 7). The `failed` variable is set at 6 locations but never checked for the final exit.
